_comment: The AI agent (_shared/lua/llm/agent.lua, windows/modules/llm/agent.ahk). System 1 is fast and cheap: it only tells whether what the user types implies one of `intents`, with a probability (an LLM with system1.prompt, or Jev through its choice question). System 2 is slow and smart: it turns a text into at most system2.max_actions actions of the closed `actions` schema, as a JSON array after system2.tag. Nothing the model writes is ever executed as is: every action is validated field by field, and a shortcut must name one of the user's own tools. Dates are local wall-clock times written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. learning bounds how accepting or dismissing a suggestion moves the per-app threshold of its intent. system1 and system2 settings (llm.agent_system1 / llm.agent_system2) name a backend like the vision actions: "local" (Ollama) or a provider of api_providers.json, optionally followed by |model; without a model, the local backend uses default_models.local and a provider its default_model in api_providers.json (the one source of provider defaults); a backend with neither needs the model.

system1.prompt:
You triage what a user is typing for a keyboard assistant. TEXT is the sentence being typed in {app}.
Decide whether it asks for, or clearly implies, one action the assistant could prepare:
- calendar: a meeting or an event at a given time
- reminder: something to remember or to do later
- mail: an email to write or to send
- shortcut: one of the user's shortcuts: {tools}
- none: anything else, including plain conversation
Reply with exactly two lines — nothing else:
INTENT: <none|calendar|reminder|mail|shortcut>
PROBABILITY: <a number from 0 to 1>

jev.instructions: Which action does the user's text ask for, or clearly imply?

criteria.none: Plain conversation or anything that needs no action
criteria.calendar: A meeting or an event at a given time
criteria.reminder: Something to remember or to do later
criteria.mail: An email to write or to send
criteria.shortcut: Running one of the user's named shortcuts
